## Problem 1 - OOP Programming

### (a) For the waldCI class, define the following:

```{r}
# define the waldCI class
setClass(
  "waldCI",
  slots = c(
    level = "numeric",
    bounds = "numeric",
    sterr = "numeric"
  )
)
# check waldCI objects have valid calues
setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {

  if (length(object@level) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(object@level) ||
      object@level <= 0 ||
      object@level >= 1) {
    return("level must be a finite number between 0 and 1")
  }

  if (length(object@bounds) != 2) {
    return("bounds must contain two values")
  }

  if (any(!is.finite(object@bounds))) {
    return("Infinite CI not supported")
  }

  if (object@bounds[1] > object@bounds[2]) {
    return("lower bound must be less than upper bound")
  }

  if (length(object@sterr) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(object@sterr)) {
    return("standard error must be finite")
  }

  if (object@sterr <= 0) {
    return("standard error must be positive")
  }

  TRUE
})
```

```{r}
# create a waldCI object
  makeCI <- function(level,
                   lb = NULL,
                   ub = NULL,
                   mean = NULL,
                   sterr = NULL) {

  if (!is.numeric(level) ||
      length(level) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(level) ||
      level <= 0 ||
      level >= 1) {
    stop("level must be between 0 and 1")
  }

  use_bounds <- !is.null(lb) || !is.null(ub)
  use_stats <- !is.null(mean) || !is.null(sterr)

  if (use_bounds && use_stats) {
    stop("Provide either lb/ub or mean/sterr, not both")
  }

  if (!use_bounds && !use_stats) {
    stop("Provide either lb/ub or mean/sterr")
  }

  z <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2)

  # Create the CI from lower and upper bounds
  if (use_bounds) {

    if (is.null(lb) || is.null(ub)) {
      stop("Both lb and ub must be provided")
    }

    if (lb > ub) {
      stop("lb must be less than ub")
    }

    if (!is.finite(lb) || !is.finite(ub)) {
      stop("Infinite CI not supported")
    }

    sterr <- (ub - lb) / (2 * z)

    return(
      new(
        "waldCI",
        level = level,
        bounds = c(lb, ub),
        sterr = sterr
      )
    )
  }

  # Create the CI from mean and standard error
  if (is.null(mean) || is.null(sterr)) {
    stop("Both mean and sterr must be provided")
  }

  if (!is.finite(sterr)) {
    stop("Infinite CI not supported")
  }

  if (sterr <= 0) {
    stop("standard error must be positive")
  }

  lb <- mean - z * sterr
  ub <- mean + z * sterr

  new(
    "waldCI",
    level = level,
    bounds = c(lb, ub),
    sterr = sterr
  )
}
```

'show' method

```{r}
# show method for waldCI object
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {

  cat(
    round(object@level * 100),
    "% CI: (",
    object@bounds[1],
    ", ",
    object@bounds[2],
    ")\n",
    sep = ""
  )

  invisible(object)
})
```

Setters:

```{r}
# update confidence level
setGeneric("level<-", function(object, value) {
  standardGeneric("level<-")
})

setMethod("level<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {

  makeCI(
    level = value,
    mean = mean(object),
    sterr = sterr(object)
  )
})


# update mean

    sterr = sterr(object)
  )
})

# update standard error
setGeneric("sterr<-", function(object, value) {

setMethod("sterr<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
```

contains and overlaps

```{r}
# check whether a value is inside the CI
setGeneric("contains", function(ci, value) {
  standardGeneric("contains")
})

setMethod("contains", "waldCI", function(ci, value) {

  stopifnot(is.numeric(value), length(value) == 1)

  value > lb(ci) & value < ub(ci)
})


# check whether two CIs overlap
setGeneric("overlap", function(ci1, ci2) {
  standardGeneric("overlap")
})

setMethod(
  "overlap",
  signature(ci1 = "waldCI", ci2 = "waldCI"),
  function(ci1, ci2) {

    max(lb(ci1), lb(ci2)) <=
      min(ub(ci1), ub(ci2))
  }
)
```

as.numeric:

```{r}
setGeneric("as.numeric")

setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x) {x@bounds})
```

transform:

```{r}
# apply a monotonic transformation to a CI
transformCI <- function(ci, fn) {

  stopifnot(is(ci, "waldCI"))
  stopifnot(is.function(fn))

  # check the function over points inside the interval
  x <- seq(lb(ci), ub(ci), length.out = 200)
  y <- fn(x)

  if (!is.numeric(y) ||
      length(y) != length(x) ||
      any(!is.finite(y))) {
    stop("The transformation must return finite numeric values")
  }

  d <- diff(y)

  increasing <- all(d >= -1e-10)
  decreasing <- all(d <= 1e-10)

  if (!increasing && !decreasing) {
    stop("The transformation must be monotonic over the CI")
  }
  new_bounds <- sort(fn(c(lb(ci), ub(ci))))

  makeCI(
    level = level(ci),
    lb = new_bounds[1],
    ub = new_bounds[2]
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| error: true

# negative standard error
makeCI(.9, mean = 3, sterr = -2)

# lower bound greater than upper bound
makeCI(.9, lb = 5, ub = 2)

# infinite bounds
makeCI(.9, lb = 2, ub = Inf)

# invalid use of setters

lb(ci1) <- 30
sterr(ci1) <- -2
sterr(ci1) <- Inf
```

## Problem 2 - data.table

```{r}
library(data.table)
tennis_dt <- fread(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farhadGithub/tennis-atp-data/main/data/raw/atp_matches_2019.csv"
)
```

### (a) How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
# combine all Davis Cup matches under one tournament name
tennis_dt[
  ,
  tournament := fifelse(
    grepl("^Davis", tourney_name),
    "Davis Cup",
    tourney_name
  )
]

# count unique tournaments
uniqueN(tennis_dt$tournament)
```

There were 69 unique tournaments in 2019.

### (b) Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
# count tournament wins for each player
champion <- tennis_dt[
  round == "F",
  .(titles = .N),
  by = winner_name
][
  titles > 1
][
  order(-titles)
]

# number of players with multiple titles
nrow(champion)

# Player(s) with the most titles
champion[titles == max(titles)]
```

Yes. 12 players won more than one tournament. Novak Djokovic and Dominic Thiem had the most tournament wins, with 5 each.

### (c) Do winners have more aces than losers?

```{r}
# ace difference within each match
ace_diff <- tennis_dt[
  !is.na(w_ace) & !is.na(l_ace),
  w_ace - l_ace
]

# mean difference
obs_diff <- mean(ace_diff)

obs_diff
```

```{r}
set.seed(506)

a <- 5000

# randomly flip winner/loser labels within each match
perm_diff <- replicate(
  a,
  mean(
    ace_diff *
      sample(c(-1, 1),
             length(ace_diff),
             replace = TRUE)
  )
)

# one-sided p-value
p_value <- (
  sum(perm_diff >= obs_diff) + 1
) / (a + 1)

p_value
```

The test provides evidence that winners have more aces than losers on average.

### (d) Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. (Note that this is NOT asking for the highest number of wins.) Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
# create one row for every player appearance
players <- rbindlist(
  list(
    tennis_dt[
      ,
      .(
        player = winner_name,
        win = 1L
      )
    ],
    tennis_dt[
      ,
      .(
        player = loser_name,
        win = 0L
      )
    ]
  )
)

# calculate matches and win rate
winrates <- players[
  ,
  .(
    matches = .N,
    winrate = mean(win)
  ),
  by = player
][
  matches >= 5
][
  order(-winrate)
]

# players with the highest win rate
winrates[winrate == max(winrate)]
```
Rafael Nadal had the highest win rate among players who played at least five matches, with a win rate of approximately 87%.

## Problem 3 - plotly

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)
library(lubridate)

covid <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/refs/heads/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv")

covid$date <- ymd(covid$date)

names(covid)[names(covid) == "date"] <- "Date"
names(covid)[names(covid) == "state"] <- "State"
```

```{r}
# state-level averages to get the national daily average
covid_us <- covid %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarize(
    cases = sum(cases_avg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### (a) How many major and minor spikes in cases were there?

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
plot_ly(
  covid_us,
  x = ~Date,
  y = ~cases,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  fill = "tozeroy",
  line = list(width = 1.5),
  hovertemplate = paste(
    "Date: %{x}",
    "<br>Average daily cases: %{y:,.0f}",
    "<extra></extra>"
  )
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "COVID-19 Cases in the United States",
    xaxis = list(title = "Date"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Average Daily Cases"),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```
There are about four major spikes in the national COVID-19 case trend and several smaller spikes. The largest spike occurred in early 2022, while other major increases appeared around late 2020, late 2021, and mid-2022.

ChatGPT helped me figure out a more briefly way to show my result.

### (b) For the states with the highest and lowest overall rates per population, what differences do you see in their trajectories over time?

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
# calculate an overall case-rate measure for each state
state_rate <- covid %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarize(
    overall_rate =
      sum(cases_avg_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
highest_state <- 
  state_rate$State[
    which.max(state_rate$overall_rate)
  ]

lowest_state <- state_rate$State[
    which.min(state_rate$overall_rate)
  ]

highest_state
lowest_state
```

```{r}
compare_data <- covid %>%
  filter(
    State %in%
      c(highest_state, lowest_state)
  )
```

```{r}
plot_ly(
  compare_data,
  x = ~Date,
  y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
  color = ~State,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",

    )
  )
```
Rhode Island has the highest overall case rate, while Maine has the lowest.

### (c) Identify, to the best of your ability without a formal test, the first five states to experience Covid in a substantial way.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
# find when each state first crossed 20 cases per 100k
first_sub <- covid %>%
  filter(
    Date >= as.Date("2020-03-01"),
    Date <= as.Date("2020-05-31"),
    cases_avg_per_100k >= 20
  ) %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  slice_min(
    order_by = Date,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

first_sub <- first_sub %>%
  mutate(
    State = factor(
      State,
      levels = rev(State)
    )
  )

plot_ly(
  first_sub,
  x = ~Date,
  y = ~State,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 13),
  text = ~paste(
    State,
    "<br>First date above 20/100k:",
    Date,
    "<br>Rate:",
    round(cases_avg_per_100k, 1)
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) %>%
  layout(
    title =
      "Earliest States to Reach Substantial COVID-19 Case Rates",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "First Date Above 20 Cases per 100k"
    ),
    yaxis = list(title = ""),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```
Using 20 average daily cases per 100,000 as a visual guideline for a substantial outbreak, the first 5 places to reach this level were New York, New Jersey, Louisiana, Connecticut, and Guam. New York reached this threshold first, followed by New Jersey and Louisiana, while Connecticut and Guam crossed it in early April 2020.
